# CourseListServer Documentation (`src/app/academy/CourseListServer.tsx`)

## Overview

The `CourseListServer` (`src/app/academy/CourseListServer.tsx`) component fetches and displays a list of courses from an API endpoint. It is a server component, meaning it fetches the data on the server before rendering the component. The `CourseList` component is wrapped in an `ErrorBoundary` to handle errors.

## Functionality

- **Fetches Courses from API:** Fetches a list of courses from the API endpoint defined in the `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` environment variable.
- **Displays Course List:** Renders a list of courses using the `CourseList` component.

## Technical Details

- The component is a server component, meaning it fetches the data on the server before rendering the component.
- The component uses the `cachedFetch` function to make the API request.
- The component dynamically constructs the base URL for the API endpoint based on the environment (development or production). In development, it uses `http://localhost:3000`, and in production, it uses `https://wescode.vercel.app`.

## Components

- `CourseListServer`: The main component that fetches and displays the list of courses.
- `CourseList`: A component that renders the list of courses.

## Data Flow

1.  The `CourseListServer` component is rendered.
2.  The component calls the `fetchCourses` function to fetch the list of courses from the API endpoint.
3.  The `fetchCourses` function makes an API request to the endpoint defined in the `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` environment variable.
4.  The API returns a list of courses.
5.  The `CourseListServer` component then renders the `CourseList` component within an `ErrorBoundary`, passing the list of courses as the `courses` prop.
6.  The `CourseList` component renders a list of courses, displaying the title, description, duration, and level of each course.

# Academy Content Update Process

This document outlines the process for updating content in the ScaleSmart Academy and details the data storage mechanisms.

## Content Creation

1.  Create new content as MDX files in the `src/app/content/academy` directory.
2.  Ensure each file includes the following metadata:
    - `title`: The title of the module.
    - `description`: A brief description of the module.
    - `moduleType`: The type of module (`article`, `video`, `exercise`, `caseStudy`, `quiz`, `simulation`).

## Content Integration

1.  Import the new MDX files into the relevant course component.
2.  Update the course's module list to include the new module.

## Content Review

1.  All content updates must be reviewed and approved by the content team.
2.  Ensure the content is accurate, up-to-date, and relevant.

## Content Updates

1.  Regularly review existing content to ensure it remains accurate and up-to-date.
2.  Update content as needed to reflect changes in the Amazon marketplace.

## Data Structures and Storage

Academy data, including courses and module progress, is primarily stored and managed using IndexedDB for robust client-side persistence.

### IndexedDB Tables

The following tables in IndexedDB are used for Academy data:

- **`courses`**: Stores `Course` objects, which represent the available courses in the academy. Each course has a unique ID, title, description, duration, level, and metadata (category, tags).
  - **Schema:** `id, title, description, duration, level, metadata.category, metadata.tags, creationTimestamp, updateTimestamp`
- **`moduleProgress`**: Stores `ModuleProgressRecord` objects, tracking the completion status and progress for each module per user. This table uses a composite primary key `[userId+courseId+moduleId]`.
  - **Schema:** `[userId+courseId+moduleId], progress, lastUpdated`

### Data Operations (IndexedDB)

The `src/lib/indexeddb-service.ts` file provides the core functions for interacting with the IndexedDB for Academy data:

- `createCourse(courseData: Course)`: Adds a new course to the `courses` table.
- `getCourse(id: string)`: Retrieves a specific course by its ID.
- `getAllCourses()`: Retrieves all courses from the `courses` table.
- `updateCourse(course: Course)`: Updates an existing course.
- `deleteCourse(id: string)`: Deletes a course by its ID.
- `deleteCoursesByIds(ids: string[])`: Deletes multiple courses by their IDs.
- `updateModuleProgress(userId: string, courseId: string, moduleId: string, progress: number)`: Updates a user's progress for a specific module.
- `getModuleProgress(userId: string, courseId: string, moduleId: string)`: Retrieves a user's progress for a specific module.
- `getCourseModuleProgress(userId: string, courseId: string)`: Retrieves all module progress records for a given user and course.

## Components and Hooks

### `useAcademyStorage` Hook

The `useAcademyStorage` hook (located in `src/hooks/use-academy-storage.ts`) is responsible for managing the academy data. It abstracts the IndexedDB operations and provides a convenient interface for components to interact with course data and module progress.

### Activity Components (e.g., `Quiz`)

Components like `Quiz` (if applicable) interact with the `moduleProgress` table via the `useAcademyStorage` hook to store and retrieve quiz results and completion status.

### `ClientCourseList` Component

The `ClientCourseList` component is responsible for rendering the list of courses. It fetches course data using the IndexedDB service functions and displays courses based on `filter` and `sort` props.

### `startCourseAction` Function

The `startCourseAction` function is used to initiate the process of starting a course. It is available through the `AcademyContext` and is used to set the active course, potentially interacting with IndexedDB to log course access or initial progress.

# Admin Page Documentation (`src/app/admin/page.tsx`)

## Overview

The Admin Page (`src/app/admin/page.tsx`) serves as the secure entry point for administrative functionalities within the application. It ensures that only authorized users can access the admin dashboard.

## Functionality

- **User Authentication:** Verifies the user's authentication status using Supabase.
- **User Authorization:** Checks if the authenticated user possesses the required authorization (specifically, a matching GitHub username configured in the application).
- **Unauthorized Access Handling:** Automatically redirects users who are not authenticated or authorized to the application's home page, ensuring security.
- **Admin Dashboard Display:** Renders the administrative dashboard for successfully authenticated and authorized users.

## Technical Details

- **Supabase Integration:** Utilizes the `@supabase/supabase-js` library to interact with the Supabase backend for authentication.
  - `createClient`: Initializes the Supabase client using environment variables (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`).
  - `getSession`: Fetches the current user session from Supabase authentication.
- **Next.js Redirection:** Employs `next/navigation`'s `redirect` function to programmatically send unauthorized users to a different route.
- **Environment Variables:** Relies on environment variables for secure configuration of Supabase credentials and the authorized GitHub username.

## Components

- `AdminPage`: The primary React component responsible for rendering the admin interface and handling authentication/authorization logic.
- `Header`: (Optional) A common header component that might be included on the admin page for consistent navigation.
- `Button`: A reusable UI component from `components/ui/button` used for various actions within the admin dashboard.

## Data Flow

1.  The `AdminPage` component is requested and begins rendering on the server.
2.  It asynchronously calls `getSession()` to retrieve the current user's Supabase session.
3.  Upon receiving the session data, it performs two checks:
    - Verifies if a `session.user` object exists (authentication check).
    - Compares `session.user.user_metadata?.user_name` against a predefined `yourGitHubUsername` (authorization check).
4.  If either the authentication or authorization check fails, the `redirect('/')` function is invoked, sending the user to the homepage.
5.  If both checks pass, the component proceeds to render the `Admin Dashboard` content, granting access to administrative features.

# Amazon Seller Tools Page Documentation

## Overview

The Amazon Seller Tools page (`src/app/amazon-seller-tools/page.tsx`) is a comprehensive dashboard designed for Amazon sellers. It allows users to upload Amazon Business Report data in CSV format, visualize key performance indicators (KPIs), analyze trends, and access specialized tools for keyword research, listing optimization, financial calculations, PPC analysis, and competitor research.

## Key Features

- **CSV Data Upload and Mapping:** Upload and map CSV files to predefined DashboardMetrics fields.
- **Dashboard Visualization:** KPI cards and data tables for visualizing metrics.
- **Time Granularity Control:** Aggregate data daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, or yearly.
- **Time Range Filtering:** Filter data by specific time ranges.
- **Period-over-Period Comparison:** Compare key metrics across different periods.
- **Specialized Tool Suite:** Tools organized into tabs for Keywords, Listing Optimization, Financials, PPC & Ads, and Competition.
- **Data Export:** Export processed data as CSV.
- **Print and Download PDF:** Share dashboard insights easily.
- **Sample Data:** Load sample data to explore functionality without uploading personal data.
- **Keyword Performance Overview Table:** Toggleable table for granular keyword performance insights.

## How to Use the Overview Dashboard

1. **Navigate to the Page:** Access via main navigation.
2. **Upload CSV Data:** Click "Upload CSV" and select your file.
3. **Map CSV Columns:** Use the OverviewDataMapper to map CSV columns to DashboardMetrics fields.
4. **View Dashboard:** Interact with charts, tables, and filters to analyze data.
5. **Interact with Data:** Sort, filter, export, and refresh data as needed.

## Data Models & Interfaces

### DashboardMetrics Interface

The dashboard processes uploaded data into a standardized `DashboardMetrics` object for each data row/period. Key fields include:

- `date`
- `sales`
- `orders`
- `conversionRate`
- `acos`
- `roas`

### CampaignData Interface

The dashboard processes uploaded data and manual input into a standardized `CampaignData` object. Key fields include:

- `campaignName`
- `adSpend`
- `sales`
- `impressions`
- `clicks`

## Specialized Tool Tabs

- **Keywords:** Tools for keyword research and analysis.
- **Listing Optimization:** Tools to improve product listings.
- **Financials:** Calculators for financial metrics.
- **PPC & Ads:** Tools for managing and auditing PPC campaigns.
- **Competition:** Tools for analyzing competitors.

## ACoS Calculator Details

The ACoS Calculator (`src/components/amazon-seller-tools/acos-calculator.tsx`) calculates the Advertising Cost of Sales. It allows manual data input and displays ACoS and RoAS.

### Input Methods

- **Manual Entry:** Enter data for a single campaign using the `ManualCalculationForm` component.

### Manual Calculation Form

The `ManualCalculationForm` component includes fields for:

- `Campaign Name`
- `Ad Spend ($)`
- `Sales ($)`
- `Impressions`
- `Clicks`
- `Clear History`

### ACoS Rating Guide

The `AcosRatingGuide` component displays ratings for interpreting ACoS values:

- **Excellent:** ACoS < 15%
- **Good:** 15% ≤ ACoS ≤ 25%
- **Okay:** 25% < ACoS ≤ 35%
- **Poor:** ACoS > 35%

### Calculation History Table

The `CalculationHistoryTable` component displays:

- `Campaign`
- `Date`
- `Ad Spend`
- `Sales`
- `ACoS`
- `RoAS`

### ACoS Trend Chart

The `AcosTrendChart` component visualizes ACoS over time using a line chart.

## Core Components

### ReusableChart Component

The `ReusableChart` component renders various types of charts.

**Props:**

- `sortedMetrics`
- `granularity`
- `chartType`
- `xAxisDataKey`
- `yAxisDataKeys`
- `colors`
- `labels`
- `title`
- `yAxisFormatter`
- `tooltipFormatter`
- `timeRange`
- `setTimeRange`
- `events`

### DashboardHeader Component

The `DashboardHeader` component displays the header for the dashboard.

**Props:**

- `isLoading`
- `isParsing`
- `error`
- `metricsLength`
- `handleRefresh`
- `handleExport`
- `metrics`
- `onSearch`

### OverviewTab Component

The `OverviewTab` component handles CSV upload, data mapping, and displays charts and data summaries.

**Props:**

- `metrics`
- `setMetrics`
- `isLoading`, `setIsLoading`
- `isParsing`, `setIsParsing`
- `isUploading`, `setIsUploading`
- `isMapping`, `setIsMapping`
- `isProcessing`, `setIsProcessing`
- `error`
- `setError`
- `TARGET_METRICS_CONFIG`
- `searchTerm`

### Button Component

The `Button` component is a reusable UI element for creating buttons.

**Props:**

- `children`
- `onClick`
- `className`

## Technical Overview

- **Frontend:** TypeScript and React (Next.js).
- **UI Components:** ShadcnUI components.
- **Charting:** Recharts library.
- **CSV Parsing:** PapaParse library.
- **Date Manipulation:** date-fns library.
- **State Management:** React hooks.
- **IndexedDB:** Local data storage.
- **Supabase:** Cloud storage for configurations.
- **Logging:** Added to `handleDownloadSampleCsv` function.

## Utility Functions

- `src/lib/amazon-tools/acos-calculator-utils.ts`
- `src/lib/utils/amazon/data-aggregation.ts`
- `src/lib/utils/amazon/data-transformation.ts`
- `src/lib/utils/formatting.ts`

# Academy Article API Endpoint Documentation (`src/app/api/academy-article/[slug]/route.ts`)

## Overview

The Academy Article API endpoint (`src/app/api/academy-article/[slug]/route.ts`) retrieves academy articles from MDX files based on their slug. It reads the MDX file, parses the frontmatter, serializes the content, and returns the serialized MDX source and frontmatter as a JSON response.

## Functionality

- **Retrieves Academy Articles by Slug:** Retrieves academy articles from MDX files based on their slug.
- **Parses Frontmatter:** Parses the frontmatter from the MDX file.
- **Serializes MDX Content:** Serializes the MDX content using `next-mdx-remote/serialize`.
- **Returns JSON Response:** Returns the serialized MDX source and frontmatter as a JSON response.

## Technical Details

- The endpoint uses the `fs` module to read the MDX file.
- The endpoint uses the `matter` library to parse the frontmatter.
- The endpoint uses the `next-mdx-remote/serialize` library to serialize the MDX content.
- The endpoint uses the `NextResponse` object from `next/server` to return the JSON response.
- The endpoint defines the directory where the MDX blog/article content is stored.

## Data Flow

1.  A request is made to the `/api/academy-article/[slug]` endpoint, where `[slug]` is the slug of the academy article.
2.  The endpoint validates the slug to ensure it only contains allowed characters (alphanumeric, hyphens, and underscores).
3.  The endpoint reads the MDX file from the file system.
4.  The endpoint parses the frontmatter from the MDX file using the `matter` library.
5.  The endpoint serializes the MDX content using the `next-mdx-remote/serialize` library.
6.  The endpoint returns the serialized MDX source and frontmatter as a JSON response.

# Academy Article API Documentation (`src/app/api/academy-article/[slug]/route.ts`)

## Overview

The Academy Article API (`src/app/api/academy-article/[slug]/route.ts`) is responsible for fetching article content for the academy modules. It retrieves the content from MDX files stored in the `src/app/content/academy` directory.

## Functionality

- **Retrieves Article Content:** The API fetches the content of an MDX file based on the provided slug.

## Technical Details

- The API uses the `fs` module to read the MDX file.
- It constructs the file path by joining the `academyDirectory` with the slug and the `.mdx` extension.
- It returns the file content in the response.

## Request

### Endpoint

`/api/academy-article/[slug]`

### Method

`GET`

### Parameters

- `slug`: The slug of the article to retrieve. This is a required parameter and should match the name of the MDX file (without the extension) in the `src/app/content/academy` directory.

## Response

### Success

- **Status Code:** `200 OK`
- **Content Type:** `application/json`
- **Body:**

```json
{
  "content": "string" // The content of the MDX file.
}
```

### Error

- **Status Code:** `500 Internal Server Error`
- **Content Type:** `application/json`
- **Body:**

```json
{
  "error": "Failed to load article"
}
```

## Example

### Request

`/api/academy-article/example-article`

### Response

```json
{
  "content": "# Example Article Content"
}
```

# Academy Courses API Endpoint Documentation (`src/app/api/academy-courses/route.ts`)

## Overview

The Academy Courses API endpoint (`src/app/api/academy-courses/route.ts`) is responsible for reading academy course data, including metadata and content, from MDX files stored in the `c:\Users\johnw\portfolio\src\app\content\academy` directory.

## Functionality

- **Reads and Serves Course Data:** Fetches all MDX files from `c:\Users\johnw\portfolio\src\app\content\academy`, parses their frontmatter (metadata) using `gray-matter`, and potentially includes the MDX content itself.
- **Provides Standardized Course Information:** Returns a structured list of courses with standardized metadata fields.

## Technical Details

- The endpoint uses the `NextResponse` object from `next/server` to return the JSON response.
- The endpoint reads MDX files from the `c:\Users\johnw\portfolio\src\app\content\academy` directory.
- Metadata is parsed from the MDX frontmatter using `gray-matter`.
- The endpoint uses the `Cache-Control` header for caching.

## Data Flow

1.  A request is made to the `/api/academy-courses` endpoint.
2.  The endpoint reads all MDX files from `c:\Users\johnw\portfolio\src\app\content\academy`.
3.  For each file, it parses the frontmatter (metadata) and extracts the MDX content.
4.  The endpoint returns an array of course objects, including their metadata and potentially the MDX content, as a JSON response.

## Request Methods

### `GET`

Returns a list of academy courses from MDX files located in `c:\Users\johnw\portfolio\src\app\content\academy`.

#### Query Parameters

- `slug` (optional): If provided, returns only the course with the specified slug.

#### Success Response

- **Code:** 200 OK

#### Example

````json
[
  {
    "slug": "example-course",
    "title": "Example Course",
    "description": "This is an example course.",
    "duration": "1h 30m",
    "level": "Beginner",
    "category": "Amazon Basics",
    "tags": ["FBA", "Product Listing"],
    "author": "ScaleSmart Team",
    "interactive": false,
    "content": "## Module 1: Introduction to SEO",
    "modules": [
      {
        "slug": "module-1",
        "title": "Module 1: Introduction",
        "content": "MDX content for module 1..."
      }
    ]
  }
]

### `POST`

Creates a new academy course.

#### Request Body

```json
{
  "title": "New Course Title",
  "description": "New course description",
  "duration": "2h 0m",
  "level": "Intermediate",
  "category": "Marketing",
  "tags": ["SEO", "Content Marketing"],
  "author": "Marketing Team",
  "interactive": true,
  "content": "## Module 1: Introduction to SEO"
}
````

#### Success Response

- **Code:** 201 Created
- **Content:**

```json
{
  "message": "Course created successfully",
  "slug": "new-course-title"
}
```

### `PUT`

Updates an existing academy course.

#### Request Body

```json
{
  "title": "Updated Course Title",
  "description": "Updated course description",
  "duration": "2h 30m",
  "level": "Advanced",
```

#### Success Response

```json
}
```

### `DELETE`

Deletes an academy course.

#### Request Body

```json

}
```

#### Success Response

- **Code:** 200 OK
- **Content:**

```json
{
  "message": "Course deleted successfully",
  "slug": "course-to-delete"
}
```

# Amazon Competitor Analysis API Endpoint Documentation (`src/app/api/amazon/competitor-analysis/route.ts`)

## Overview

The Amazon Competitor Analysis API endpoint (`src/app/api/amazon/competitor-analysis/route.ts`) performs competitor analysis based on uploaded CSV data. It processes the CSV data, extracts metrics, and currently returns static case study data.

## Functionality

- **Processes CSV Data:** Processes uploaded CSV data for seller and competitor information, converting it into a structured format.
- **Extracts Metrics (Internal):** Extracts specified metrics (e.g., price, reviews) from the processed CSV data internally for analysis.
- **Returns Static Response:** Currently returns static 'case-studies' data as a JSON response. Note that the internally extracted competitor metrics are not currently included in the API response.

## Technical Details

- The endpoint uses the `zod` library to validate the request body.
- It expects CSV data containing headers like `asin`, `price`, `reviews`, `rating`, `conversion_rate`, and `click_through_rate`.
- The `processCSVData` function (defined within [`src/app/api/amazon/competitor-analysis/route.ts`](src/app/api/amazon/competitor-analysis/route.ts)) is used to parse the CSV data, handling type conversions for numerical fields and defaulting invalid numbers to 0.
- The `loadStaticData` function is used to fetch static case study data, which is currently returned by the API.

## Request Body

The API accepts a `POST` request with a JSON body containing the following parameters:

| Parameter        | Type       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Required | Example                                          |
| :--------------- | :--------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------- | :----------------------------------------------- |
| `sellerData`     | `string[]` | An array of strings, where each string is a line from the CSV file representing the seller's product data. The first line should be the header row.                                                                                                            | Yes      | `["asin,price,reviews", "B09ABCDEFG,25.99,150"]` |
| `competitorData` | `string[]` | An array of strings, where each string is a line from the CSV file representing competitor product data. The first line should be the header row.                                                                                                              | Yes      | `["asin,price,reviews", "B08HIJKLM,24.50,300"]`  |
| `metrics`        | `string[]` | (Optional, but recommended for internal processing) An array of strings specifying which metrics to extract from the CSV data (e.g., "price", "reviews", "rating"). If provided, metrics are processed internally, but not currently returned in the response. | No       | `["price", "reviews"]`                           |
| `asin`           | `string`   | (Optional) A single ASIN for direct product analysis. While accepted, the primary analysis currently relies on `sellerData` and `competitorData` CSV uploads.                                                                                                  | No       | `"B07ZYW34RT"`                                   |

### Example Request

```json
POST /api/amazon/competitor-analysis
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "sellerData": [
    "asin,price,reviews,rating,conversion_rate,click_through_rate",
    "B09ABCDEDF,25.99,150,4.2,0.05,0.02"
  ],
  "competitorData": [
    "asin,price,reviews,rating,conversion_rate,click_through_rate",
    "B08HIJKLM,24.50,300,4.5,0.06,0.03",
    "B07QRSTUV,26.00,100,4.0,0.04,0.01"
  ],
  "metrics": ["price", "reviews", "rating"]
}
```

## Response

Upon successful processing, the API currently returns a JSON object containing static 'case-studies' data.

### Success Response Example (200 OK)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "title": "Case Study: Optimizing Listing Images for Higher Conversion",
      "slug": "optimizing-listing-images",
      "date": "2023-03-10",
      "content": "This case study examines how optimizing product images on Amazon led to a 15% increase in conversion rate for a new electronics product."
    },
    {
      "title": "Case Study: Leveraging Customer Reviews for Product Improvement",
      "slug": "leveraging-customer-reviews",
      "date": "2023-04-01",
      "content": "An analysis of how feedback from Amazon customer reviews can be effectively used to refine product features and increase customer satisfaction."
    }
  ]
}
```

### Error Response Example (400 Bad Request / 500 Internal Server Error)

```json
{
```

## 1. High-Level System Architecture

This project is built using the Next.js framework, leveraging its capabilities for both frontend rendering and backend API routes. The application's architecture is broadly categorized into:

- **Frontend (UI/UX):** Developed with React.js components and Next.js for server-side rendering (SSR) and static site generation (SSG) where appropriate, ensuring a fast and responsive user experience.
- **Backend (API Routes):** Implemented using Next.js API routes (`src/app/api/**/*.ts`), serving as the interface for client-side requests and handling business logic. These routes interact with external services and the database.
- **Database:** Supabase serves as the primary data store, offering a PostgreSQL database, authentication services, and real-time capabilities. This choice provides a robust and scalable backend foundation.
- **Authentication:** Managed via NextAuth.js, integrated with GitHub OAuth for secure user registration and sign-in.
- **Content Management:** Markdown (`.mdx`) files are used for documentation and blog content, providing a flexible and developer-friendly way to manage static content.

The core principle behind this architecture is a modular, scalable, and secure application that can evolve efficiently.

## 2. Authentication and Authorization

This section details the implementation of user registration and sign-in, including API endpoints, the authentication flow, and data models.

### 2.1 API Endpoints

- **/api/register**: This endpoint initiates the user registration process by redirecting to the configured OAuth provider (GitHub). It acts as a gateway to the external authentication service.
- **/api/sign-in**: Similar to registration, this endpoint facilitates user sign-in by redirecting to the GitHub OAuth provider.
- **/api/auth/[...nextauth]**: This is the dynamic catch-all route managed by NextAuth.js. It handles all authentication-related callbacks (e.g., OAuth redirects), session management, and user data persistence with the database.

### 2.2 Authentication Flow

1.  **User Initiation**: A user attempts to register or sign in by navigating to `/api/register` or `/api/sign-in` (or clicking a respective UI button).
2.  **OAuth Redirection**: The application redirects the user to the GitHub OAuth provider's authorization page. This offloads authentication to a trusted external service.
3.  **GitHub Authentication**: The user authenticates directly with GitHub, granting permission for the application to access their profile information.
4.  **Authorization Code Callback**: GitHub redirects the user back to the application's NextAuth.js callback URL (e.g., `/api/auth/callback/github`) with an authorization code.
5.  **Token Exchange & Profile Retrieval**: NextAuth.js intercepts this callback, exchanges the authorization code for an access token with GitHub, and retrieves the user's profile information (e.g., email, name, image).
6.  **User Synchronization (Database)**: NextAuth.js interacts with the Supabase adapter (`@next-auth/supabase-adapter`) to check for an existing user. If the user does not exist, a new user record is created in the database.
7.  **Session Creation**: A secure session is established for the authenticated user, typically stored as a cookie.
8.  **Application Redirection**: The user is finally redirected to the main application, now authenticated and ready to access protected content.

### 2.3 GitHub OAuth Integration

The application leverages [NextAuth.js](https://next-auth.js.org/) for a streamlined and secure GitHub OAuth implementation. NextAuth.js simplifies the complex aspects of authentication, including token management, session handling, and adapter integration with various databases.

Configuration involves setting up a GitHub OAuth application to obtain client ID and secret, which are then provided to NextAuth.js. The callback URL must be precisely configured to `https://your-app-domain.com/api/auth/[...nextauth]`.

### 2.4 Data Models

The `User` model is central to authentication and user management:

- **User**: Represents an authenticated user within the system. The definition, including key properties like email, name, and role, is found in [`src/lib/models/user.ts`](src/lib/models/user.ts).

  ```typescript
  export interface User {
    email: string;
    name?: string;
    image?: string;
    emailVerified?: Date;
    role: 'user' | 'admin'; // Role-based access control (RBAC) is implemented
    createdAt: Date;
    updatedAt: Date;
  }
  ```

  _Insight:_ The `role` field is crucial for implementing role-based access control (RBAC), allowing different levels of permissions within the application (e.g., 'user' for general access, 'admin' for administrative functions).

### 2.5 Database Schema

Supabase (PostgreSQL) is the chosen database. The `users` table is fundamental for storing user authentication and profile data, seamlessly integrated via the `@next-auth/supabase-adapter`.

```sql
-- Example users table schema
-- This schema aligns with NextAuth.js's default user model expectations
CREATE TABLE users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(255),
  image VARCHAR(255),
  emailVerified TIMESTAMPTZ,
  role VARCHAR(255) DEFAULT 'user',
  createdAt TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updatedAt TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

_Insight:_ Using `UUID` for `id` provides globally unique identifiers, which is a good practice for distributed systems or when merging data from different sources. The `DEFAULT NOW()` for `createdAt` and `updatedAt` simplifies timestamp management.

## 3. Middleware and Public Path Management

The application employs a robust middleware (`src/middleware.ts`) for centralized authentication and authorization checks.

### 3.1 Role of Middleware

The middleware acts as a gatekeeper, intercepting requests before they reach Next.js pages or API routes. Its primary responsibilities include:

- **Authentication Check**: Verifying the presence and validity of an authentication token (session).
- **Authorization**: Ensuring that authenticated users have the necessary permissions (e.g., based on their `role`) to access specific resources.
- **Redirection**: Redirecting unauthenticated or unauthorized users to designated pages (e.g., sign-in or a 403 Forbidden page).

### 3.2 Public Paths Configuration

A crucial aspect of the middleware's functionality is the identification of "public paths" — routes that do not require authentication. These paths are explicitly defined in [`src/config/publicPaths.ts`](src/config/publicPaths.ts). This centralized configuration promotes:

- **Maintainability**: Easily add or remove public routes without modifying core middleware logic.
- **Security**: Prevents accidental exposure of protected routes.
- **Clarity**: Provides a clear overview of publicly accessible endpoints.

### 3.3 Implementation Details

- **Token Retrieval**: The `middleware.ts` file utilizes the `getToken` function from `next-auth/jwt` to securely retrieve and parse the JSON Web Token (JWT) from the request. This token contains the user's session information.
- **Path Matching**: The `publicPaths.ts` file exports an array containing string patterns and regular expressions (`RegExp`) to flexibly define which routes are exempt from authentication checks. The middleware iteratively matches incoming request URLs against these patterns.

## Row Level Security and Policies Setup

**Key Changes Made:**

- Function Definition First: The public.validate_verification_token function is now defined before any policies that reference it, ensuring that it exists when the policies are created.

```sql
-- Enable Row Level Security for all tables
ALTER TABLE public.users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.accounts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.sessions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE public.verification_tokens ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Updated validate_verification_token Function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.validate_verification_token(token TEXT, identifier TEXT)
RETURNS BOOLEAN AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM public.verification_tokens
    WHERE public.verification_tokens.token = token
      AND public.verification_tokens.identifier = identifier
      AND public.verification_tokens.expires > NOW()
  );
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

-- Users Table Policies
CREATE POLICY "Users can select their own user data." ON public.users
AS PERMISSIVE FOR SELECT
TO public
USING (id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Users can update their own user data." ON public.users
AS PERMISSIVE FOR UPDATE
TO public
USING (id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (updated_at IS NOT NULL);  -- Restrict updates to only the updated_at field

DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can delete their own user data." ON public.users;

-- Accounts Table Policies
CREATE POLICY "Users can select accounts associated with their user ID." ON public.accounts
AS PERMISSIVE FOR SELECT
TO public
USING (user_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Users can insert accounts associated with their user ID." ON public.accounts
AS PERMISSIVE FOR INSERT
TO public
WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Users can update accounts associated with their user ID." ON public.accounts
AS PERMISSIVE FOR UPDATE
TO public
USING (user_id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (
    (oauth_token IS NULL OR oauth_token IS NOT NULL) AND
    (oauth_scopes IS NULL OR oauth_scopes IS NOT NULL)
);  -- Ensure only oauth_token and oauth_scopes can be updated

CREATE POLICY "Users can delete accounts associated with their user ID." ON public.accounts
AS PERMISSIVE FOR DELETE
TO public
USING (user_id = auth.uid());

-- Sessions Table Policies
CREATE POLICY "Users can select sessions associated with their user ID." ON public.sessions
AS PERMISSIVE FOR SELECT
TO public
USING (user_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Users can insert sessions associated with their user ID." ON public.sessions
AS PERMISSIVE FOR INSERT
TO public
WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());

-- If updates are needed, implement a similar policy as accounts
CREATE POLICY "Users can update sessions associated with their user ID." ON public.sessions
AS PERMISSIVE FOR UPDATE
TO public
USING (user_id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (TRUE);  -- Adjust as necessary to restrict specific fields

CREATE POLICY "Users can delete sessions associated with their user ID." ON public.sessions
AS PERMISSIVE FOR DELETE
TO public
USING (user_id = auth.uid());

-- Verification Tokens Table Policies
CREATE POLICY "Allow inserts for anyone." ON public.verification_tokens
AS PERMISSIVE FOR INSERT
TO public
WITH CHECK (true);  -- Consider restricting this policy

CREATE POLICY "Allow selects only for valid tokens." ON public.verification_tokens
AS PERMISSIVE FOR SELECT
TO public
USING (public.validate_verification_token(token, identifier));

-- Trigger function for users table
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.check_user_update()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
    IF NEW.id <> OLD.id OR NEW.email <> OLD.email OR NEW.created_at <> OLD.created_at THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot update id, email, or created_at fields';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

-- Trigger for users table
CREATE TRIGGER check_user_update_trigger
BEFORE UPDATE ON public.users
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.check_user_update();

-- Trigger function for accounts table
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.check_account_update()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
    IF NEW.id <> OLD.id OR NEW.user_id <> OLD.user_id OR NEW.provider_type <> OLD.provider_type OR NEW.provider_id <> OLD.provider_id OR NEW.provider_account_id <> OLD.provider_account_id OR NEW.created_at <> OLD.created_at THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot update id, user_id, provider_type, provider_id, provider_account_id, or created_at fields';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

-- Trigger for accounts table
CREATE TRIGGER check_account_update_trigger
BEFORE UPDATE ON public.accounts
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.check_account_update();
```

# Utility Functions Documentation (`src/lib/utils.ts`)

This document provides an overview and usage details for the utility functions defined in `src/lib/utils.ts`.

## `cn`

The `cn` function is a utility for conditionally joining CSS class names together. It leverages `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` to efficiently combine class strings, resolve conflicts, and ensure proper Tailwind CSS class ordering.

### Function Signature

```typescript
function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]): string;
```

### Parameters

- `inputs`: An array of `ClassValue` (which can be strings, objects, or arrays of `ClassValue`).

### Return Value

A single string containing merged and optimized CSS class names.

### Example

```typescript
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const isActive = true;
const buttonClasses = cn(
  'p-2',
  'bg-blue-500',
  isActive && 'text-white',
  { 'font-bold': isActive },
  'hover:bg-blue-700',
);
console.log(buttonClasses); // Output: "p-2 bg-blue-500 text-white font-bold hover:bg-blue-700"
```

## `generateSlug`

The `generateSlug` function generates a URL-friendly slug from a given title string. It converts the title to lowercase, replaces spaces with hyphens, removes non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens), and trims leading/trailing hyphens.

### Function Signature

```typescript
function generateSlug(title: string): string;
```

### Parameters

- `title`: The input string (title) to be converted into a slug.

### Return Value

A string representing the generated slug.

### Example

```typescript
import { generateSlug } from '@/lib/utils';

const title = 'My Awesome Course Title!';
const slug = generateSlug(title);
console.log(slug); // Output: "my-awesome-course-title"
```

## Privacy Policy

Last Updated: May 21, 2025

This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, and protect your information when you use this application.

### Data Storage

Currently, your data is stored locally within your web browser's IndexedDB. This is part of our free tier service. We do not collect or store any personal data on our servers at this time.

### Data Usage

The stored data is used solely to provide the application's core functionality and improve your user experience. We do not share your data with any third parties.

### User Rights

You have the right to access, modify, and delete your data. You can do this by clearing your browser's site data. We also encourage you to use any available "Export" features to back up your data.

### Future Plans

We are planning to introduce a paid tier with cloud storage. We will update this policy to reflect any changes in data handling practices when this feature is available.

### Third-Party Services

For the core functionality of this application, we do not utilize third-party services that collect your personal data.

We use Vercel Analytics to understand general traffic patterns and improve our website experience. Vercel Analytics collects anonymized and aggregated data, including metrics such as page views, visit durations, browser types, operating systems, and general geographic locations (derived from IP addresses but anonymized).
